TWO SUBSTANTIVE REVIEWER CONTRIBUTIONS the writer verified and accepts: (1) TestDecideEnumeratesTheFullCrossProduct still passes 10/10 with the decode sort removed, so it provides NO determinism coverage -- it covers the cross-product shape only. The writer confirmed the cause is twofold: the fixture's inputs are already in ascending ID order (decode-a, decode-b; prefill-a, prefill-b) AND the expectation loop calls sortedByID itself at policy_test.go lines 29, 31 and 32 of the function, so it mirrors the mutation away. Reviewer asks for a one-line comment saying it covers shape rather than determinism, since the current comment reads as though the replicated ordering is verified rather than assumed. (2) The P > 1 BOUNDARY, which corrects an overstatement by the writer: the committed deployment is 1P (config.md:36, --prefill-instances 1), so the prefill-axis exact tie cannot arise between two prefill pods on the shipped 1p2d topology. It goes live only in the topology sweep, which carries 2p2d and 3p1d (verified by the writer at sim_results/topology/capacity_selection.json, and README:108-109 cites that sweep for the 0.0100-against-0.0800 result). The writer's 'steady state under decode-side congestion' phrasing could be read as already biting on the shipped fleet; it is latent there and active only when P > 1. Reviewer recommends stating this next to the D1 regime note in config.go's estimatorRollforward doc, with a cross-reference from doc.go's D1 paragraph, and continuing to claim no direction. Reviewer also confirmed the algebra: on the disaggregated branch every prefill-endpoint-dependent term feeds remoteLeadUs while cXferUs is request-dependent, and both surviving terms after the max are decode-side only, so when tAdmD dominates J is identical BIT-FOR-BIT across prefill candidates rather than merely within tolerance -- which is why the tie is exact and why the old map-scan was flaky rather than merely fragile.
